what: Brinker International owns Chili's and Maggiano's Little Italy, operating about 1,600 restaurants, mostly company-owned, in the United States and through franchises abroad.
customers: American families and groups eating out at casual dining prices.
money: the Italian chain and international franchise royalties
moat: A turnaround built on running fewer promotions, simplifying the menu and advertising value against fast food, which lifted traffic sharply while rivals lost it.
risks: Casual dining traffic is cyclical and the recent gains came from a specific marketing campaign
Beef and labour costs have both risen
17 times earnings after the shares already rose a great deal
opportunities: Revenue grew from $3.8B to $5.8B in four years, nearly all from traffic rather than new restaurants
$601M of free cash flow and an 8.4% net margin, high for casual dining
Analysts see about 39% upside, with 22 covering the stock
watch: Chili's comparable restaurant traffic, which is what the whole story rests on.
